actions.title: List 3 things you can do that others might pay for
actions.description: Write down 3 skills or tasks you can do—from cleaning to tech help to advice. Don't overthink it. Just write.

actions.title: Find 5 local organizations offering free services
actions.description: Search online or ask around for food banks, job centers, free clinics, or community centers near you. Save their contact info.

actions.title: Apply to 3 jobs on Indeed or local job boards
actions.description: Pick 3 jobs you can do and apply. Don't wait for the perfect match. Apply now, improve later.

actions.title: Register for a free online course
actions.description: Go to Coursera, Khan Academy, or YouTube and sign up for one free course in something useful or interesting to you.

actions.title: Map free internet locations near you
actions.description: Find libraries, coffee shops, community centers, or public wifi spots. Write down their addresses and hours.

actions.title: Call 2 people you haven't spoken to in 6 months
actions.description: Reach out. Not to ask for anything—just to reconnect. Relationships matter more than you think.

actions.title: Check if you qualify for local assistance programs
actions.description: Look up SNAP, housing assistance, unemployment, or local aid programs. See what you're eligible for.

actions.title: Update your phone contact list
actions.description: Add useful numbers: job centers, help lines, friends who offered support. Delete numbers you don't need.

actions.title: Write a 1-paragraph bio about yourself
actions.description: Describe who you are and what you can do in 3-4 sentences. Keep it simple. You'll use this later.

actions.title: Document 1 thing you did today that worked
actions.description: Write it down. Anything—big or small. This builds a record of what you're capable of.

actions.title: Visit 3 local businesses and ask if they're hiring
actions.description: Go in person. Ask to speak to a manager. Even if they say no, you're practicing and building presence.

actions.title: Set up a free Google Voice number
actions.description: Get a dedicated number for job applications and opportunities. Keep your personal number separate.

actions.title: Create a basic resume using Google Docs
actions.description: Use a free template. List your experience, skills, and contact info. One page is fine. Done is better than perfect.

actions.title: Identify 5 online platforms where you can offer services
actions.description: Look into TaskRabbit, Fiverr, Upwork, local Facebook groups, or Nextdoor. See where your skills fit.

actions.title: Walk or transit to 3 new neighborhoods
actions.description: Explore areas you don't usually go to. Notice businesses, community centers, and opportunities you didn't know about.

actions.title: Find 3 free skill-building events this month
actions.description: Check Meetup, Eventbrite, library calendars, or community boards for workshops, talks, or training sessions.

actions.title: Join 5 relevant online groups or forums
actions.description: Find Reddit communities, Facebook groups, or Discord servers related to your interests or job goals. Lurk first, engage later.

actions.title: Create a list of 10 small problems you've solved
actions.description: Think back on times you figured something out—at work, home, or anywhere. Write them down. These are your skills.

actions.title: Research 3 gig economy apps available in your area
actions.description: Check if you can drive for Uber/Lyft, deliver for DoorDash/Instacart, or do tasks on other apps. Know your options.

actions.title: Spend 2 hours at the library
actions.description: Use free internet, browse job boards, read, or just be somewhere quiet and focused. Libraries are underrated resources.

actions.title: Complete 1 free certification course online
actions.description: Find a short certification on Google, LinkedIn Learning, or Coursera. Finish it. Add it to your resume.

actions.title: Learn 10 new words or terms in an industry you want to enter
actions.description: Read articles, watch videos, or join forums. Write down terms you don't know and look them up. Language builds credibility.

actions.title: Watch 5 YouTube tutorials on a specific skill
actions.description: Pick one skill—editing, coding, design, repair—and watch 5 videos about it. Take notes. Try it yourself.

actions.title: Practice explaining what you do in 30 seconds
actions.description: Write it out, then say it out loud. You'll use this in interviews, networking, and random conversations.

actions.title: Read 3 articles about a topic you want to understand better
actions.description: Pick something relevant to your goals. Read deeply. Take notes. This is how you build real knowledge.

actions.title: Teach someone something you know
actions.description: Explain a skill, a process, or something you're good at to someone else. Teaching clarifies your own understanding.

actions.title: Follow 10 people in your target industry on LinkedIn or Twitter
actions.description: Find professionals doing what you want to do. Follow them. Read what they share. Learn how they think.

actions.title: Write 5 questions you'd ask someone in a job you want
actions.description: Think about what you need to know. Write thoughtful questions. This prepares you for real conversations.

actions.title: Practice a hard conversation out loud
actions.description: Pick a tough topic—asking for help, negotiating pay, setting boundaries. Say it out loud alone. Practice matters.

actions.title: Track 1 habit for 7 days
actions.description: Pick one small thing—drinking water, walking, reading—and track it daily for a week. Build evidence that you follow through.
